item.text:
No reused web evidence from the prior thread.

New evidence below is limited to the strongest cross-chapter items I retained after checking roughly 30 documents and collapsing duplicates, rewrites, and weak commentary pieces.

1. MOFA says nuclear safety/security is a national responsibility and that the NCA chaired by the PM controls nuclear security.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Arms Control And Disarmament","publisher":"Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of Pakistan","publication_date":"undated; current page accessed 2026-07-20","url":"https://mofa.gov.pk/arms-control-and-disarmament","claim":"Pakistan says nuclear safety and security are a national responsibility and that the prime minister-chaired National Command Authority exercises control over nuclear security and other aspects.","locator":"section 'Nuclear Safety and Security', lines 136-137","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Current government policy page describing formal structure and stated policy; self-claim, but about institutional design rather than a contested event.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Stable institutional context for 2022 and directly relevant to Sharif's PM tenure.","ruler_attribution":"Direct for formal authority held by the PM; actual operational control still sits inside an institutional and military hierarchy.","contrary_evidence":["This is a government self-description, not independent verification of day-to-day practice."],"lenses":["1B.3","1B.7","1B.10"]}

2. MOFA says Pakistan backed CTBT, is a CTBTO observer, keeps a unilateral testing moratorium, and will not be first to resume testing in South Asia.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Arms Control And Disarmament","publisher":"Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of Pakistan","publication_date":"undated; current page accessed 2026-07-20","url":"https://mofa.gov.pk/arms-control-and-disarmament","claim":"Pakistan says it consistently supported the CTBT, participated in negotiations, is an accredited CTBTO observer state, observes a unilateral moratorium on nuclear testing, and will not be the first to resume testing in South Asia.","locator":"section 'Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty (CTBT)', lines 128-130","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Current official policy page with explicit treaty posture and testing moratorium language.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Stable posture relevant to 2022 and to Sharif's inherited nuclear environment.","ruler_attribution":"Mostly inherited state policy; it constrains but does not by itself prove Sharif personally advanced disarmament.","contrary_evidence":["Pakistan is still a non-signatory, so this is policy support rather than binding treaty commitment."],"lenses":["1B.1","1B.4","1B.10"]}

3. NTI summarizes the NCA as Pakistan's top nuclear decision body and says military dominance can reassert itself in crisis.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"National Command Authority (NCA)","publisher":"Nuclear Threat Initiative","publication_date":"undated; current page accessed 2026-07-20","url":"https://www.nti.org/education-center/facilities/national-command-authority-nca/","claim":"The NCA is Pakistan's highest decision-making authority on nuclear and missile policy, but NTI notes that in wartime or a military crisis the military would probably prevail; the chairmanship moved from the president to the prime minister in 2009.","locator":"about section, lines 60-62","source_type":"scholarship","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Independent specialist source summarizing long-standing Pakistani command-and-control structure and expert caution about crisis behavior.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Long-running structure still governing 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Direct for formal PM chairmanship, limited for actual crisis control.","contrary_evidence":["The page is secondary analysis, not an official Pakistani statement; the 'probably prevail' point is an expert judgment."],"lenses":["1B.3","1B.7","1B.8","1B.10"]}

4. SIPRI's 2022 yearbook places Pakistan's arsenal at 165 warheads at the start of 2022 and says arsenals are likely to grow.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Global nuclear arsenals are expected to grow as states continue to modernize - New SIPRI Yearbook out now","publisher":"Stockholm International Peace Research Institute","publication_date":"2022-06-13","url":"https://www.sipri.org/media/press-release/2022/global-nuclear-arsenals-are-expected-grow-states-continue-modernize-new-sipri-yearbook-out-now","claim":"SIPRI estimated Pakistan's nuclear stockpile at 165 warheads at the start of 2022 and said the global trend points toward continued modernization and growth.","locator":"table 'World nuclear forces, January 2022', Pakistan row","source_type":"scholarship","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Widely used technical assessment from a leading open-source nuclear-warnings institution, with explicit quantitative estimate.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Exact target year 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Country-level inherited posture rather than Sharif-specific action.","contrary_evidence":["This is an estimate, not an official Pakistani count."],"lenses":["1B.10","1B.3"]}

5. The UN CTBT history page says Pakistan has yet to sign the CTBT.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"End Nuclear Tests Day - History","publisher":"United Nations","publication_date":"undated; current page accessed 2026-07-20","url":"https://www.un.org/en/observances/end-nuclear-tests-day/history","claim":"The UN says India, DPRK, and Pakistan have yet to sign the CTBT.","locator":"history section on CTBT status","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Direct UN status summary for the treaty regime; stable and non-controversial on signature status.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Stable legal context for 2022.","ruler_attribution":"State-level constraint, not a Sharif-specific act.","contrary_evidence":["Not signing the CTBT does not by itself show intent to test."],"lenses":["1B.4","1B.10"]}

6. MOFA rejected TPNW obligations as not binding on Pakistan.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Entry into Force of the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons","publisher":"Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of Pakistan","publication_date":"2021-01-29","url":"https://mofa.gov.pk/press-releases/entry-into-force-of-the-treaty-on-the-prohibition-of-nuclear-weapons","claim":"Pakistan said it does not consider itself bound by the TPNW's obligations and does not treat the treaty as part of customary international law.","locator":"closing paragraph, lines 123-123","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Direct foreign-ministry statement of Pakistan's treaty position.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Pre-2022 but still operative in 2022 as the standing position.","ruler_attribution":"Inherited state policy; useful mainly as a constraint on 2022 arms-control options.","contrary_evidence":["This is a negative treaty posture and does not by itself prove active escalation."],"lenses":["1B.4","1B.10"]}

7. Reuters reporting on Sharif's election describes the 2022 transition as a constitutional crisis in a politically turbulent nuclear-armed state.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Pakistan parliament elects Sharif PM as Khan MPs quit en masse","publisher":"Reuters via Euronews","publication_date":"2022-04-12","url":"https://www.euronews.com/2022/04/12/us-pakistan-politics","claim":"Reuters said parliament chose Shehbaz Sharif after a no-confidence vote in a week-long constitutional confrontation, and that the nuclear-armed country was likely to remain prone to political and economic turbulence.","locator":"paragraphs around lines 594-596","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters wire reporting, but the article is a short political summary rather than a nuclear-policy document.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Exact accession period in April 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Context for inherited constraints, not proof of nuclear conduct.","contrary_evidence":["This is broad political context, not direct evidence of nuclear decision-making."],"lenses":["1B.7","1B.10"]}

8. Reuters analysts said Sharif had amicable military ties and would not act with complete independence.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Sharif, frontrunner as next Pakistani PM, seen as 'can-do' administrator","publisher":"Reuters via Euronews","publication_date":"2022-04-10","url":"https://www.euronews.com/2022/04/10/us-pakistan-politics-sharif","claim":"Reuters reported that analysts said Shehbaz Sharif enjoyed amicable relations with Pakistan's military, which traditionally controls foreign and defence policy, and that he would not act with complete independence because he would need to work on a collective agenda with coalition partners.","locator":"paragraphs around lines 666-678","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters-derived analysis about power structure and governing constraints, not a direct nuclear record.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly relevant to the start of Sharif's 2022 tenure.","ruler_attribution":"Directly relevant to the limits on his authority over security policy.","contrary_evidence":["The source is analytical and not a formal institutional record."],"lenses":["1B.7","1B.8","1B.10"]}

9. Sharif's letter to Modi in April 2022 sought peaceful, cooperative ties and regional peace and security.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"PM Shehbaz writes letter to Modi, says peaceful Pak-India ties imperative for progress of region","publisher":"Dawn","publication_date":"2022-04-17","url":"https://www.dawn.com/news/1685458/pm-shehbaz-writes-letter-to-modi-says-peaceful-pak-india-ties-imperative-for-progress-of-region","claim":"Sharif wrote to Narendra Modi saying Pakistan remained committed to regional peace and security and that peaceful and cooperative ties were imperative for regional progress.","locator":"article summary and quoted letter excerpt","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Mainstream local reporting with a quoted letter, but still a secondary source rather than the underlying diplomatic note.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Exact April 2022 accession phase.","ruler_attribution":"Direct Sharif diplomatic signaling.","contrary_evidence":["The overture did not produce a structural thaw in 2022."],"lenses":["1B.1","1B.8"]}

10. Reuters reported India's accidental missile firing into Pakistan and the absence of casualties.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"India says it accidentally fired missile into Pakistan","publisher":"Reuters via Yahoo News","publication_date":"2022-03-11","url":"https://news.yahoo.com/india-says-accidentally-fired-missile-131702096.html","claim":"Reuters reported that India said a technical malfunction during routine maintenance accidentally fired a missile into Pakistan and that there was no loss of life.","locator":"lead paragraph","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters wire reporting with a clear contemporaneous account of the incident and its immediate safety outcome.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Exact March 2022 crisis context immediately before Sharif took office.","ruler_attribution":"Inherited external crisis context; not Sharif's own act, but central to the 2022 safety environment.","contrary_evidence":["The source concerns India's error, so it cannot be used as proof of Sharif's conduct."],"lenses":["1B.8","1B.10"]}

11. Pakistan's Islamabad Declaration called for a joint probe after the missile incident and framed Pakistan as an anchor of stability.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Islamabad Declaration","publisher":"Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of Pakistan","publication_date":"2022-03-23","url":"https://mofa.gov.pk/islamabad-declaration","claim":"The declaration expressed grave concern over the 9 March 2022 missile incident, called on India to conduct a joint probe with Pakistan, and described Pakistan as an anchor of stability in South Asia committed to non-use or threat of use of force and pacific settlement of disputes.","locator":"paragraph 15 and paragraph 16","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Official multilateral declaration hosted by MOFA with explicit text on crisis handling and restraint.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Exact 2022 crisis-response context.","ruler_attribution":"Directly relevant to the Sharif government's diplomatic handling of a dangerous incident, though the declaration is not sole proof of his personal command decisions.","contrary_evidence":["Multilateral declaratory language can be aspirational and may overstate actual operational control."],"lenses":["1B.1","1B.8","1B.10"]}

12. Shehbaz publicly rejected Biden's nuclear remark and invoked responsible stewardship, command and control, and IAEA safeguards.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"PM rejects US President's remarks about Pakistan's nuclear assets","publisher":"Radio Pakistan","publication_date":"2022-10-15","url":"https://www.radio.gov.pk/15-10-2022/pm-rejects-us-presidents-remarks-about-pakistans-nuclear-assets","claim":"Shehbaz Sharif rejected Joe Biden's remarks, said Pakistan was a responsible nuclear state, and described its programme as managed through a technically sound command and control system with IAEA-level safeguards.","locator":"article text and embedded tweet quote, lines 36-47","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Official government broadcaster carrying the PM's own statement; good for attribution but still self-assertion, not independent verification.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Exact October 2022 period.","ruler_attribution":"Direct Sharif rhetoric and self-presentation on nuclear stewardship.","contrary_evidence":["This is a self-description and not independent proof that safeguards improved in 2022."],"lenses":["1B.2","1B.3","1B.8","1B.10"]}

13. MOFA's public line on the March missile incident emphasized restraint and peaceful settlement norms.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Pakistan rejects India's purported closure of the incident of the firing of a supersonic missile into Pakistani territory on 9 March 2022 and reiterates demand for joint probe","publisher":"Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of Pakistan","publication_date":"2022-08-24","url":"https://mofa.gov.pk/pakistan-rejects-indias-purported-closure-of-the-incident-of-the-firing-of-a-supersonic-missile-into-pakistani-territory-on-9-march-2022-and-reiterates-demand-for-joint-probe","claim":"Pakistan said the Indian missile incident had jeopardized regional peace and that Pakistan's response showed exemplary restraint and an abiding commitment to peace as a responsible nuclear state.","locator":"press release body, opening paragraphs","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Official post-incident foreign-office statement with explicit wording about restraint and strategic-stability concerns.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly within the 2022 period and about a key crisis event.","ruler_attribution":"Relevant to Sharif's government line, though it is still an institutional foreign-office statement rather than a private PM decision record.","contrary_evidence":["This is a self-serving diplomatic statement and should be checked against independent reporting."],"lenses":["1B.8","1B.10","1B.1"]}

**Search and rejection summary**
I reviewed roughly 30 documents across official Pakistani pages, UN/CTBTO/IAEA pages, SIPRI, NTI, Reuters wires and syndications, Dawn, the Indian Express, AP, Al Jazeera, Tribune, The Guardian, and other regional coverage.

I rejected or deprioritized items that were:
- duplicates of the same Reuters wire on the March 2022 missile incident,
- generic opinion pieces or explainers that added no new factual claim,
- out-of-period or mostly retrospective material when a 2022 source was available,
- weak fact-checks or social-media explainers that did not improve attribution,
- broad economic or flood stories that were useful for other chapters but not for 1B,
- inaccessible cache-miss pages or repeated pages that added no new evidence.

Examples of collapsed/removed clusters:
- Multiple March 2022 missile-incident articles from Reuters-syndicated outlets were reduced to one independent incident source plus one Pakistani official response source.
- Older FAS Pakistan notebook items were considered but not retained because they were pre-2022 background and less useful than SIPRI/NTI for this chapter.
- Several generic peace-or-diplomacy articles about India or the US were not retained because they did not add nuclear-specific authority, restraint, or safety detail.

**Remaining gaps**
- No direct 2022 evidence surfaced of a Shehbaz-chaired NCA meeting focused on nuclear doctrine, custody, or safety reform.
- No independent source showed a substantive change to Pakistan's launch posture, command-and-control rules, or fissile-material policy under Sharif in 2022.
- There is still no material evidence that Sharif personally handled dual-use cyber, biological, or AI risk policy in 2022.
- Evidence for 1B.6 and part of 1B.7 remains thin: I found no strong 2022 example of Sharif resisting proliferation pressures or appointing expert nuclear reformers in a way that can be cleanly attributed to him.

Net takeaway, without scoring: Sharif had formal nuclear-chairmanship authority and publicly projected restraint, but the 2022 record I found is mostly inherited-posture management and crisis de-escalation signaling, not proof of structural risk reduction.
